Every omitted key falls back to messages/uz.json via the deep-merge in src/i18n/request.ts. STILL UZBEK ON PURPOSE, do not fill these in without a verified source: the seven keys that lead with the operator's registered name (footer.operator and the about/duties/structure/news/sold/contact metaDescriptions) need the organisation's OFFICIAL name in this language, not a rendering invented here; minRates.pageLede is the title of a Vazirlar Mahkamasi decision and needs its official wording. Statutory content (the 24 privileges, the Markaz documents) is not in this file at all — it lives in the database and is deliberately untranslated.

stats.title: Statistics
stats.lede: Results of the {year} electronic auctions for {scope}
stats.unavailable: The statistics service is currently unavailable. Please try again later.
stats.valueNote: Annual lease value is the sum of one year's lease payments on the lots leased. It is not a sale price: state property is leased, not sold.
stats.monthlyBody: The bars are the number of lots leased in the month. The dashed line is the average lot price that month. An average, not a total: a single large lot can move a whole month.
stats.outcomeBody: Every lot is in one of three states: leased, at auction, or cancelled.
stats.riseBody: Final price as a ratio of the starting price
stats.byPerM2: Average price per 1 m² per year (up to 100 m²)
stats.perM2Note: Objects up to 100 m² only — 68 % of all auctions fall in that band. The cap is necessary: in some regions more than half of what is leased is natural water bodies and open land, which cost a few soʻm per 1 m² and distort the building rate completely. A region needs at least 20 measurements.
stats.sizeNote: Most of the group above 1000 m² is natural water bodies. They are few in number but enormous in area: a single lot reaches 48 million m². Areas are therefore never summed on this page, and the typical (median) value is used rather than the mean — otherwise the “ordinary” lot would come out at five hectares.
stats.recordsBody: Lots with a starting price above 1 million soʻm are included in the largest-rise list
stats.riseFloor: Lots with a starting price above 1 million soʻm are included in the largest-rise list.
stats.registerBody: This comes from a different service and does not match the auctions above: the register also counts contracts extended without an auction.
stats.scatterNote: Each circle is one region. Horizontal axis: how many lots were leased. Vertical axis: what 1 m² costs (for objects up to 100 m²). Circle size is that region's annual lease value. The two measures do not agree: the region that leased the most lots is not the most expensive one.
stats.contractsByRegionNote: The register's own figures, ordered by size. This is not a time axis — do not read it as growth from left to right.
stats.oneStepNote: The share of lots leased in the 1.0–1.5× band — the most common case.
stats.tenPlusNote: Lots leased at more than ten times the starting price.
stats.cumulativeNote: Each point is the share of lots leased at least that many times above the starting price.
stats.avgRiseNote: The mean of the final price as a ratio of the starting price.
stats.metaDescription: Auction statistics for leasing state property — by region, by month, and price trends.
